To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

amiodarone, although it may be more efficacious than other drugs for the treatment of patients with drug‐resistant ventricular tachycardias, is not more efficacious than a drug selected to be effective on the basis of electrophysiologic testing.
empiric AM was no more effective than “ineffective” drugs in patients with drug refractory VT/VF.
empiric amiodarone is not more effective than ineffective drug therapy in patients with refractory ventricular tachycardia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs for the treatment of cardiovascular disorders and the study of the mechanisms of action of drugs already in clinical use.
the development of new methods of treatment of ventricular arrhythmia.
the study of the mechanisms of the action of amiodarone and the evaluation of its clinical use in patients with refractory ventricular arrhythmias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the study are consistent with the results of the previous studies.
empiric amiodarone is not superior to an ineffective drug selected based on electrophysiologic testing.
amiodarone is a drug that has a place in the armamentarium for the treatment of patients with refractory ventricular arrhythmias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
empiric AM therapy in patients with VT/VF refractory to other antiarrhythmic drugs is no better than therapy with drugs predicted to be ineffective by EP studies.
amiodarone is not the drug of choice in patients with drug refractory VT/VF.
the efficacy of empiric amiodarone in patients with drug-refractory arrhythmia is not superior to that of drugs predicted ineffective in electrophysiological studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amiodarone is no more efficacious than ineffective drugs in patients with drug-refractory VT/VFs.
empiric therapy with AM does not improve the prognosis of patients with drug‐resistant VT/VF.
amiodarone is not a panacea.
